text.en: How much salt can 100 ml of water hold before it stops dissolving?

The aim is to test the solubility of a salt by observing saturated and unsaturated solutions at a given temperature. A saturated solution cannot dissolve more solute at that temperature.
Pour 100 ml of water in a 250 ml beaker and add table salt from three packets of 25 g, 11 g and 1 g one after another with constant stirring, observing whether each dissolves.
Record whether the salt dissolved or not and infer whether the solution is unsaturated, saturated or supersaturated. The amount at which no more dissolves is the amount needed for saturation.
